| **Full-quality render of a DRAFT video made in this chat** | `enhance_video` | "make this draft full quality", "finalize the draft", "render the draft I picked" — every trigger requires a draft from `generate_video(draft: true)`; nothing else routes here |
| **Change what is IN a finished video** | `edit_video` | "remove the X from this video", "replace the sign", "make it look like 16mm film", "turn day into night", "change her jacket to red", "edit this video" |
| **Make a finished video sharper / bigger** | `upscale_video` | "upscale this", "make it 4K", "higher resolution", "sharper", "clean this clip up" |
| **Everything else (T2I, edits, inpainting, style transfer, multi-reference, object swap)** | `generate_image` | every other prompt |

If the user's message contains a try-on intent — even subtly, e.g. "I want to try red Nike sportswear" or "what do I look like in this jacket" — `vto` is the right tool. "Try-on" is broader than clothing: adding or swapping ANY wearable item (hat, sunglasses, glasses, shoes, bag, jewelry) using a reference image of that item is a try-on, and so is replacing one worn item with another ("replace her hat with this one"). The subject doesn't have to be human — dressing a pet or mascot in a garment still routes to `vto`; don't switch back to `generate_image` mid-flow because the subject is an animal. Do NOT default to `generate_image` and describe the item in prose; the try-on endpoint preserves face and pose much better than prompt-only edits (which visibly alter faces). See the **Virtual Try-On** section below for the full flow (it includes a web-search step for sourcing brand garments).

## Video mode selection (`generate_video`)

`generate_video` takes a `requests` array (up to 4 entries, each one video — batch multi-video asks into ONE call, like `generate_image`). Each entry picks an explicit `mode`, and user-provided media MUST go in the matching mode's field — NEVER describe provided media in prose and call with `t2v` (the model invents everything from scratch and the result will look unrelated to the user's media):

| Text only, no media | `mode: "t2v"` |
| Animate a single image / bring this picture to life | `mode: "i2v"`, `keyframes: [{image}]` |
| Transition / morph / interpolate BETWEEN two images | `mode: "i2v"`, `keyframes: [{image}, {image}]` (first = opening frame, second = closing frame) |
| Storyboard through 3-10 images | `mode: "i2v"`, one keyframe per image + explicit `duration` — or per-keyframe `timestamp` (seconds, all-or-none) to pin exact positions; with timestamps `duration: "auto"` runs the clip to the last timestamp |
| Continue / extend an existing clip | `mode: "v2v"`, `start_video` (chain calls to go past 20s) |
| Keep this subject consistent / c… [truncated]

]# frame.md · Dixi demo film design truth

**Concept angle:** "A century of adapting, then one calm cockpit." The history plays in warm, dark archival tones. The film then opens into Dixi's light, precise UI world, where a living workflow map shows which step is running.

## Palette (Dixi tokens, light canvas)
- bg `#f5f7fb` (soft, blue-tinted, never pure white) · surface `#ffffff`
- ink `#0d1b2a` · ink-soft `#3b4a5c` · muted `#6b7a8f` · line `#d5dde8`
- L1 `#0f3d75` · L2 `#1c69d4` · L3 `#5aa9f0` (depth of blue = strength of a layer)
- human `#e22718`: **only** for human decisions (PM gate, reject, memory loop)
- markets: CN `#e0483a` · US `#0f3d75`
- History scenes (s1, s2 opening): dark archival stage `#0b1220` with warm grain. This is the deliberate exception that makes the cut to light feel like "today".

## Type
- Display: **Instrument Serif** 400 (and italic) for story titles and years. Large: 96–220px.
- UI / labels / body: **Geist Sans** 400/500/700. Labels 22–26px, body 30–40px.
- Mono: **Geist Mono** 500 for the terminal close, scores and timestamps.

## Components
- **App window**: recordings sit in a floating window (radius 22px, 2px line border, deep soft shadow), with a slim title bar showing the URL `dixi · /dashboard/cn/5-series`.
- **Workflow map**: Mermaid-style flowchart. Rounded nodes, 3px edges. The active node fills with its layer colour and glows, and edges draw on. Two modes: a full-frame pop (≈3 s) and a corner mini-map (bottom-right, 520×300) that keeps the active node lit.
- **AI-generated label**: a small pill "AI-generated" on every FLUX image (EU AI Act Art. 50).
- **Credit line**: 18px muted text at the bottom-left on history photos (author · licence).

## Motion
- Eases: `power3.out` for entrances, `expo.inOut` for camera moves, `back.out(1.6)` only for node pops.
- Punch-ins on the recording: scale 1.0 → 1.35 toward the click, then back.
- Never more than one moving focus at a time. Calm and minimalist.

## Don'ts
- No BMW logos (none generated). No gradient text, no neon.
- Red is never decoration.
# Dixi screen recordings for the pitch video

Recorded 2026-10-11 from the real app (`pnpm build && pnpm start`, production server, so there is no dev overlay). Light mode, viewport 1920x1080 at DPR 1, headless Chrome.
Capture method: CDP screencast at JPEG q92 with real frame timestamps, converted to MP4 (H.264, yuv420p tv-range, 30 fps CFR, CRF 16).
A cursor dot (22 px, semi-transparent dark, white rim) and a blue click ripple are injected because headless video has no cursor. Over the dark car banners the dot reads as a white ring.

**Data:** fictional demo set `Demo/02-data/demo-pipeline.json`, built by `Demo/02-data/build-demo-pipeline.mjs`. It contains no BMW data and no real quotes. The banner therefore says **"Example data"** (origin `example`), not "BMW hackathon data". No fallback banner appears for China: CN has 1,840 comments in the demo set.

]# frame.md · Dixi demo film design truth

**Concept angle:** "A century of adapting, then one calm cockpit." The history plays in warm, dark archival tones. The film then opens into Dixi's light, precise UI world, where a living workflow map shows which step is running.

## Palette (Dixi tokens, light canvas)
- bg `#f5f7fb` (soft, blue-tinted, never pure white) · surface `#ffffff`
- ink `#0d1b2a` · ink-soft `#3b4a5c` · muted `#6b7a8f` · line `#d5dde8`
- L1 `#0f3d75` · L2 `#1c69d4` · L3 `#5aa9f0` (depth of blue = strength of a layer)
- human `#e22718`: **only** for human decisions (PM gate, reject, memory loop)
- markets: CN `#e0483a` · US `#0f3d75`
- History scenes (s1, s2 opening): dark archival stage `#0b1220` with warm grain. This is the deliberate exception that makes the cut to light feel like "today".

## Type
- Display: **Instrument Serif** 400 (and italic) for story titles and years. Large: 96–220px.
- UI / labels / body: **Geist Sans** 400/500/700. Labels 22–26px, body 30–40px.
- Mono: **Geist Mono** 500 for the terminal close, scores and timestamps.

## Components
- **App window**: recordings sit in a floating window (radius 22px, 2px line border, deep soft shadow), with a slim title bar showing the URL `dixi · /dashboard/cn/5-series`.
- **Workflow map**: Mermaid-style flowchart. Rounded nodes, 3px edges. The active node fills with its layer colour and glows, and edges draw on. Two modes: a full-frame pop (≈3 s) and a corner mini-map (bottom-right, 520×300) that keeps the active node lit.
- **AI-generated label**: a small pill "AI-generated" on every FLUX image (EU AI Act Art. 50).
- **Credit line**: 18px muted text at the bottom-left on history photos (author · licence).

## Motion
- Eases: `power3.out` for entrances, `expo.inOut` for camera moves, `back.out(1.6)` only for node pops.
- Punch-ins on the recording: scale 1.0 → 1.35 toward the click, then back.
- Never more than one moving focus at a time. Calm and minimalist.

## Don'ts
- No BMW logos (none generated). No gradient text, no neon.
- Red is never decoration.

## Re-recording
Everything is in `_tools/` (`pnpm install` there; it uses the system Chrome via Playwright 1.49.1):
1. `cp ../../02-data/demo-pipeline.json ../../../web/data-local/pipeline.json`, then `cd web && pnpm build && pnpm start`.
2. `WANT_LEADER="Comfort & craft" node take-cn.mjs` (rec-01…05, about 90 s; exit code 3 means the social leader differed, so run it again), `node take-weights.mjs` (rec-06), `node take-us.mjs` (rec-07). Each take clears all `dixi:*` localStorage first.
3. `node reencode.mjs` rebuilds every MP4 from the saved frames in `_frames/` (about 800 MB; delete it if you don't need re-encodes).
4. Restore the real data: `cp ../../02-data/backup/pipeline.real.json ../../../web/data-local/pipeline.json && cmp …`, then `pnpm build` again.
`_tools/sim.ts` (`npx tsx sim.ts`) checks the demo data offline against the app's own scoring and profile logic.

content.content:
Hear every market. Decide with a reason.

--- **Dixi** helps BMW product managers decide what the next car should offer. It listens to customers in every market, weighs what they say, and turns it into clear requirements. Every requirement keeps the reason it was chosen. *Named after the Dixi 3/15, BMW's first car (1928).* ## How Dixi thinks: three layers Not every input counts the same. Dixi sorts what it knows into three layers, from strongest to weakest. | | Layer | What goes in | How much it counts | |---|---|---|---| | 🟦 | **L1 · BMW principles** | The fundamentals of each series, owned by named managers. *Example: "The 7 Series puts rear-seat luxury first."* | Strongest. Every profile is checked against them. | | 🔵 | **L2 · Market evidence** | Customer feedback and feature requests, customer studies, sales, today's option list. A research agent adds competitor features people like and market trends, each with its sources. | The main engine. | | 🩵 | **L3 · Social test** | Runs only after profiles exist: which generated profile tracks better on social media (simulated for now). | Weakest, and set per series: 7 Series 2 %, 5 Series 8 %, 1 Series 20 %. | ## From customer voice to car profiles, in five steps 1. **Choose.** Pick a market on the globe, then a series (1, 5 or 7). 2. **Analyse.** AI reads the BMW principles and the market evidence, and builds one list of feature requests by category (Exterior, Interior, Digital, Powertrain) and urgency. 3. **Decide.** The product manager **keeps or rejects** each request (a reject always needs a reason), drags the list into priority order, and stars competitor features or trends onto a wishlist. Every decision records who and when. 4. **Build.** Dixi builds three car profiles (*Fix the basics*, *Tech-forward*, *Comfort & craft*) that follow the PM's priority. Each one exports as a catalogue-style PDF. 5. **Remember.** Each build is saved as a **generation** with its profiles, decisions and priority. Run the social test (L3) on it, or edit and rebuild. ```mermaid flowchart LR M[Market + series] --> A[AI analysis
L1 principles · L2 evidence
+ research agent] A --> H{{Product manager
keep · reject with reason
priority · wishlist}} H --> P[3 car profiles
follow the PM's priority] P --> G[(Generation
profiles · decisions · who · when)] G --> S[L3 social test
low weight] S -. "updates scores" .-> G G -. "edit and rebuild" .-> H ``` **Dixi is honest about what it doesn't know.** Missing markets, thin samples and conflicting signals are shown to the product manager, not hidden. ## Run it ```bash cd web pnpm install pnpm dev ``` Open http://localhost:3000, or see it live at **https://dixi-wheat.vercel.app**. Full setup (Supabase CLI, Vercel, Entire): [`docs/requirements.md`](docs/requirements.md). ## What's in the repo | Folder | What | |---|---| | [`web/`](web/) | The app: landing page with a live market globe, the requirement pipeline and the generations dashboard | | [`backend/`](backend/) | API and AI agents (planned) | | [`docs/`](docs/) | Setup, architecture diagrams, tech stack | | [`branding/`](branding/) | Logo, colours, brand guide | | [`scripts/`](scripts/) | Image generation, and the local data build for the pipeline | --- Built for the BMW challenge "AI for Product Decision Making" at the EHL Hackathon, Munich, October 2026. Dixi is a hackathon project and is not affiliated with BMW. # Dixi backend (planned) Not built yet. This folder will hold the API and the AI agents behind the dashboard. Today the web app runs on typed sample data in `web/src/lib/`. ## Planned stack Python · **FastAPI** · **Pydantic AI** (agents with typed outputs) · **Supabase** (Postgres + pgvector) · **OpenAI**. Details and alternatives: `../docs/tech-stack/README.md`. Architecture: `../docs/architecture/`. ## Planned layout ``` backend/ ├── app/ │ ├── main.py FastAPI app, routes │ ├── api/ /markets, /requirements, /decisions, /lineage, /weights, /principles, /gaps │ ├── agents/ labeller, clusterer, requirement writer, prioritiser, scribe (Pydantic AI) │ ├── scoring/ Dixi score (demand · market backing · principle fit) + decision memory (see docs/architecture/09) │ ├── models/ Pydantic data contracts (Evidence, Requirement, Decision, Principle, Gap, …) │ └── db/ Supabase client, migrations ├── tests/ └── pyproject.toml managed with uv ``` ## Decision memory (must-have for the agents) Before the requirement agent proposes feature requests for a series and market, it calls `get_decision_memory(series, market)`: past decisions with who, when, reason and the customer count at the time. A request that was rejected before is **not proposed again** at full strength. It comes back only when demand has grown past the team's threshold ("resurfaced"), and then the agent quotes the old reason and the change. Matching uses the request title plus pgvector similarity, so a reworded request is still recognised. The rules and weights match `web/src/lib/pipeline/scoring.ts` and the team's settings (`scoring_settings` table). ## Rules - Customer data is never committed. Load it from Supabase or a local, git-ignored folder. - Secrets come from the repo-root `.env` (git-ignored). - Every agent output is typed and stored with its inputs, so each requirement can be traced back to its evidence. docs/architecture/04-build-plan.md docs/architecture/02-feedback-loop.md docs/architecture/05-hitl-map.md PM->>UI: G4 hand off to Codebeamer Codebeamer export (ReqIF / CSV) :e1, 2026-10-11 10:00, 2h handoff["Hand off to Codebeamer
AI proposes"] OR-->>UI: AI proposal "bigger (+80–120 mm)", confidence medium, Japan objection visible, gap card "Japan data thin" Evidence-gap detector + "What we don't know" panel :d3, after d2, 2h /opt/homebrew/bin/ffmpeg Demo/04-recordings/_tools: encode.mjs lib.mjs node_modules package.json pnpm-lock.yaml reencode.mjs report-cn.json report-us.json report-weights.json run-cn.log server.log sim.ts take-cn.mjs take-us.mjs take-weights.mjs weights-meta.json Demo/04-recordings/stills: cn-fridge-detail.png cn-list.png cn-profiles-after-social.png cn-profiles.png cn-reject-dialog.png cn-social.png decision-log.png us-profiles.png weights-logged.png weights.png

Full setup (Supabase CLI, Vercel, Entire): [`docs/requirements.md`](docs/requirements.md). ## What's in the repo | Folder | What | |---|---| | [`web/`](web/) | The app: landing page with a live market globe, the requirement pipeline and the generations dashboard | | [`backend/`](backend/) | API and AI agents (planned) | | [`docs/`](docs/) | Setup, architecture diagrams, tech stack | | [`branding/`](branding/) | Logo, colours, brand guide | | [`scripts/`](scripts/) | Image generation, and the local data build for the pipeline | --- Built for the BMW challenge "AI for Product Decision Making" at the EHL Hackathon, Munich, October 2026. Dixi is a hackathon project and is not affiliated with BMW. # Dixi backend (planned) Not built yet. This folder will hold the API and the AI agents behind the dashboard. Today the web app runs on typed sample data in `web/src/lib/`. ## Planned stack Python · **FastAPI** · **Pydantic AI** (agents with typed outputs) · **Supabase** (Postgres + pgvector) · **OpenAI**. Details and alternatives: `../docs/tech-stack/README.md`. Architecture: `../docs/architecture/`. ## Planned layout ``` backend/ ├── app/ │ ├── main.py FastAPI app, routes │ ├── api/ /markets, /requirements, /decisions, /lineage, /weights, /principles, /gaps │ ├── agents/ labeller, clusterer, requirement writer, prioritiser, scribe (Pydantic AI) │ ├── scoring/ Dixi score (demand · market backing · principle fit) + decision memory (see docs/architecture/09) │ ├── models/ Pydantic data contracts (Evidence, Requirement, Decision, Principle, Gap, …) │ └── db/ Supabase client, migrations ├── tests/ └── pyproject.toml managed with uv ``` ## Decision memory (must-have for the agents) Before the requirement agent proposes feature requests for a series and market, it calls `get_decision_memory(series, market)`: past decisions with who, when, reason and the customer count at the time. A request that was rejected before is **not proposed again** at full strength. It comes back only when demand has grown past the team's threshold ("resurfaced"), and then the agent quotes the old reason and the change. Matching uses the request title plus pgvector similarity, so a reworded request is still recognised. The rules and weights match `web/src/lib/pipeline/scoring.ts` and the team's settings (`scoring_settings` table). ## Rules - Customer data is never committed. Principled.
Weighted.
Traceable.

AI for product decision making · BMW × EHL Hackathon 2026

Named after BMW's first car, 1928.

1928
Dixi 3/15 · Tobias Nordhausen · CC BY 2.0
Dixi is a hackathon project and is not affiliated with BMW. All app data shown is fictional example data.
1916 → 2025

Sources: bmwgroup.com/en/company/history.html · BMW Group, "100 years" (press.bmwgroup.com, T0257819EN) · 1945 pots and pans: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_BMW (secondary source). Photos: Wikimedia Commons.
The problem

Today the change
is data.

  • What customers want is buried in comments, studies, trends and competitor moves.
  • Markets disagree, and the signals conflict.
  • The product manager must decide, stay in control, and show why.
EXAMPLE DATA · 5 SERIES
1,840
customer comments

customer comments
USA

feature requests after clustering
China
Counts are from Dixi's fictional demo dataset, not BMW data.
Two customers

Same car. Two best seats.

The best seat is in the back.
Rear spaceRear fridgeQuiet cabin
AI-generated
USA
The best seat is behind the wheel.
Sharper steeringVentilated seatsLarger trunk
Personas are fictional (FLUX images). Grounded in public facts: China 5 Series long wheelbase, +12 cm for rear comfort (press.bmwgroup.com T0427958EN); 2006 5 Series Li rear cooling box (T0009351EN).
How Dixi decides

Three layers. One human gate.

Depth of blue = strength of a layer. Red = a human decision.
Layer 1

Principles come first.

  • Years of BMW market knowledge, owned by product managers.
  • Every profile is checked against them first.
dixi · /dashboard/cn/5-series · profile
Real app screen, example data. Principles P1–P3 for the 5 Series, each with an owner.
Layer 2

Evidence, scored.

  • Feedback, trends and competitors become feature requests.
  • Every request is scored: the top is the priority.
  • Every source is one click away.
dixi · /dashboard/cn/5-series
request detail
Real app screens. Quotes and counts are fictional example data.
The human gate

A human decides.
Memory keeps it.

  • Keep, or reject with a reason. The reason is required.
  • Logged with name and time.
  • The next generation remembers it.
reject request
decisions log
Real app screens. "Marco Rossi" is a fictional demo PM.
The math · default weights, 5 Series

Simple, and yours to tune.

1 · REQUEST SCOREYour weights score every request
100 × (0.60·Demand + 0.25·Backing + 0.15·Fit) Demand = log(1+mentions) / log(1+top mentions) · Backing = competitor & trend signals, capped at 2 · Fit = 1 if in the series focus, else 0.4
Rear-seat refrigerator · China
0.60×100 + 0.25×0 + 0.15×100
= 75
2 · DECISION MEMORYA reject costs 60% next time
score × (1 − 0.60 × strength) strength = 0.5^(days / 365) · a keep adds up to +5 points · a reject comes back if demand grows ≥ 30%
Smaller footprint for city parking
52 × (1 − 0.60 × 1)
52 → 21
3 · PROFILE SCOREWhat car to build
41%·L1 + 51%·L2 + 8%·L3 L3 (social) is set per series: 8% for the 5 Series · L1 = 45% of the rest · L2 takes the remainder
Comfort & craft · China
.41×100 + .51×84 + .08×60
= 89 best fit
From the app code (web/src/lib/pipeline/scoring.ts, profiles.ts, series.ts). Weights 41/51/8 are rounded (0.414 / 0.506 / 0.08). Example: reject just made, strength 1.
Layer 3

Profiles,
then a test.

  • Three profiles from what you kept, with the why behind every spec.
  • A social test checks the response. Social is noisy, so it gets the lowest weight.
dixi · profiles · 5 Series · China
analytics · social test (simulated)
Real app screens. The social campaign is simulated: no real posts were made.
Source weights

Every weight
is yours.

  • Move a slider, or say what matters in plain words.
  • AI proposes. The PM applies.
  • Every change is logged: who, when, what.
dixi · /dashboard/settings
change log
Real app screens. Prompt: "Trust customer feedback more than social media for the 5 Series". Nothing changes until Apply.
The result

Same data. Two answers.

AI-generated

Long wheelbase, rear fridge.
Rear-seat fridge #1Rear legroom #2Quiet cabin #3
AI-generated
USA · Tech-forward · 89
A driver's car.
Sharper steering #1CarPlay #2Head-up display #3
Best-fit profiles from the app on fictional example data. Images are AI-generated (FLUX), no real cars or logos.
Traceability

Every answer has a trail.

Click any spec and walk back to the customer who asked for it.

CUSTOMER COMMENT
"I sit in the back on most trips; a small fridge for water is expected at this price."
→
FEATURE REQUEST
Rear-seat refrigerator
214 mentions · score 75
→
PM DECISION
Kept · Marco Rossi
11 Oct 2026, 03:49
→
PROFILE
Comfort & craft
priority #1 · 89, best fit
AND THE REJECTS TOO
Smaller footprint for city parking · Rejected · "Contradicts L1: rear space is core for China" · shown in every profile's decision trail
Example data: the comment, PM name and counts are fictional.
Honesty

What we don't know yet.

The data is fictional

The demo runs on an invented dataset. No BMW data and no real customer quotes are shown.

Not validated on real data

How well clustering and scores match BMW's own judgement is not measured yet.

The social test is simulated

No real posts. It is seeded, so a re-run can change which profile leads.

Weights are defaults

60 / 25 / 15, a 60% reject cost, a one-year half-life, 8% social. They need calibrating with BMW PMs.

Gaps are shown, not hidden

A market with no comments falls back to all markets and says so. "What we don't know" cards exist as a design, not yet in the pipeline.

No backend yet

Decisions live in the browser for now. FastAPI and Supabase are planned, not built.

From the repo: backend/README.md ("Not built yet"), web/src/lib/pipeline/scoring.ts, Demo/04-recordings/RECORDINGS.md.
Feasibility and next steps

Running today. Built to grow.

Today
  • Live Next.js app: dixi-wheat.vercel.app
  • Full flow: market → requests → decisions → profiles → social test
  • Plain-language weights assistant on a live AI call
  • 1, 5 and 7 Series configured; profiles export as PDF
Next
  • Backend: FastAPI, Pydantic AI, Supabase
  • Shared decision memory across teams
  • Reworded requests matched by vector similarity
  • Hand-off to Codebeamer (ReqIF / CSV)
"Next" items are plans from backend/README.md and docs/architecture/04-build-plan.md, not built yet.

How Dixi decides

Three layers. One human gate.

Depth of blue = strength of a layer. Red = a human decision.
Layer 1

Principles come first.

  • Years of BMW market knowledge, owned by product managers.
  • Every profile is checked against them first.
dixi · /dashboard/cn/5-series · profile
Real app screen, example data. Principles P1–P3 for the 5 Series, each with an owner.
Layer 2

Evidence, scored.

  • Feedback, trends and competitors become feature requests.
  • Every request is scored: the top is the priority.
  • Every source is one click away.
dixi · /dashboard/cn/5-series
request detail
Real app screens. Quotes and counts are fictional example data.
The human gate

A human decides.
Memory keeps it.

  • Keep, or reject with a reason. The reason is required.
  • Logged with name and time.
  • The next generation remembers it.
reject request
decisions log
Real app screens. "Marco Rossi" is a fictional demo PM.
The math · default weights, 5 Series

Simple, and yours to tune.

1 · REQUEST SCOREYour weights score every request
100 × (0.60·Demand + 0.25·Backing + 0.15·Fit) Demand = log(1+mentions) / log(1+top mentions) · Backing = competitor & trend signals, capped at 2 · Fit = 1 if in the series focus, else 0.4
Rear-seat refrigerator · China
0.60×100 + 0.25×0 + 0.15×100
= 75
2 · DECISION MEMORYA reject costs 60% next time
score × (1 − 0.60 × strength) strength = 0.5^(days / 365) · a keep adds up to +5 points · a reject comes back if demand grows ≥ 30%
Smaller footprint for city parking
52 × (1 − 0.60 × 1)
52 → 21
3 · PROFILE SCOREWhat car to build
41%·L1 + 51%·L2 + 8%·L3 L3 (social) is set per series: 8% for the 5 Series · L1 = 45% of the rest · L2 takes the remainder
Comfort & craft · China
.41×100 + .51×84 + .08×60
= 89 best fit

then a test.

  • Three profiles from what you kept, with the why behind every spec.

input.content:
# Dixi pitch deck

Local only (git-ignored). This deck tells the same story as the 3-minute demo film (`Demo/06-film`), in the same brand.

- `dixi-deck.html`: a self-contained 16:9 deck with 16 slides at 1920×1080. Use ←/→, space, PageUp/PageDown, Home/End or click to move. `#5` in the URL opens slide 5. Fonts and images load from `assets/`, with no network calls.
- `dixi-deck.pdf`: 16 pages, one slide per page (1920×1080 px = 1440×810 pt).
- `_contact.png`: all 16 PDF pages on one sheet, for QC.

## Slides
| # | Title | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Principled. Weighted. Traceable. | Title, subtitle, "Named after BMW's first car, 1928." (Dixi 3/15 photo) |
| 2 | BMW has always adapted. | History strip: 1916 engines, 1923 R 32, 1928 Dixi, 1945 ruins and pots and pans, 1962 Neue Klasse, 2025 iX3 |
| 3 | Today the change is data. | The problem: signals are buried and conflict, and the PM must stay in control and traceable |
| 4 | Same car. Two best seats. | China (rear seat) vs USA (driver) personas, AI-generated |
| 5 | Three layers. One human gate. | Workflow map (static SVG of the film's map): L1 → L2 → Requests → PM gate → L3 → Social test → Recommend, plus Decision memory and Source weights |
| 6 | Principles come first. | L1, owned by PMs and checked first (app screen: Why this profile + P1–P3) |
| 7 | Evidence, scored. | L2: scored request list + Rear-seat refrigerator detail with its sources |
| 8 | A human decides. Memory keeps it. | Keep, or reject with a required reason, logged with name and time (reject dialog + decisions log) |
| 9 | Simple, and yours to tune. | The three formulas with worked examples: 75 · 52 → 21 · 41/51/8 → 89 |
| 10 | Profiles, then a test. | L3: three profiles; the social test is noisy, so it gets the lowest weight |
| 11 | Every weight is yours. | Plain-language AI proposal, PM applies, change log |
| 12 | Same data. Two answers. | CN Comfort & craft 89 (fridge, legroom, quiet cabin) vs US Tech-forward 89 (steering, CarPlay, HUD) |
| 13 | Every answer has a trail. | Lineage: comment → request → PM decision → profile, and rejects stay visible |
| 14 | What we don't know yet. | Honesty: fictional data, not validated, simulated social test, default weights, gap handling, no backend yet |
| 15 | Running today. Built to grow. | What runs today vs what is planned (backend, shared memory, vector matching, Codebeamer) |
| 16 | Dixi. | Close: "btw, what was BMW's first car?" → "Dixi." · "BMW. The Ultimate Driving Machine." (credited to BMW) |

## Numbers and where they come from
- Request score = 100 × (0.60·Demand + 0.25·Backing + 0.15·Fit). Demand = log(1+m)/log(1+max), Backing = min(1, signals/2), Fit = 1 in focus, else 0.4. Source: `web/src/lib/pipeline/scoring.ts` (`DEFAULT_SCORING`, `scoreRequest`).
- Memory: reject → × (1 − 0.60 × 0.5^(days/365)); keep → + 10 × 0.5 × strength (up to 5); resurface at +30% demand. Source: same file. 52 × 0.4 = 20.8 → 21.
- Profile: w3 = 0.08 for the 5 Series (`series.ts`), w1 = 0.45 × (1 − w3) = 0.414, w2 = 0.506 (`profiles.ts`). Comfort & craft: L1 1.0, L2 518/618 = 0.838, L3 0.60 → 0.886 → 89 (91 before the social test). Matches `Demo/04-recordings/RECORDINGS.md`.
- List values (fridge 214 mentions, score 75; smaller footprint 52; CN 1,840 comments, 13 requests; US 2,960 comments; US Tech-forward 89) come from `RECORDINGS.md` and the stills. All of them are fictional demo data.

## External sources
- BMW history: https://www.bmwgroup.com/en/company/history.html
- BMW Group "100 years" PDF (R 32 and Dixi): https://www.press.bmwgroup.com/global/article/attachment/T0257819EN/354550/EN_BMW_Group_100_of_years_fascination_for_mobility.pdf
- 1945 pots and pans (secondary source): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_BMW
- China 5 Series long wheelbase, +12 cm: https://www.press.bmwgroup.com/global/article/detail/T0427958EN/the-new-bmw-5-series-sedan-and-the-new-bmw-i5-%E2%80%93-exclusively-from-china-for-china?language=en
- 2006 5 Series Li rear cooling box: https://www.press.bmwgroup.com/global/article/detail/T0009351EN/bmw-group-introducing-new-models-for-china?language=en
- "The Ultimate Driving Machine" since 1974: https://www.press.bmwgroup.com/usa/article/detail/T0447993EN_US/chapter-6:-%E2%80%9Cthe-ultimate-ad-slogan:-bmw-becomes-the-ultimate-driving-machine%E2%80%9D?language=en_US
- Repo: `backend/README.md` (backend planned, not built), `docs/architecture/04-build-plan.md` (Codebeamer ReqIF/CSV export, gap panel), `README.md` (L3 weights per series, PDF export).

## Image credits
History photos come from Wikimedia Commons. Each photo carries its credit on the slide.
- BMW IIIa · Wikisympathisant · CC BY-SA 4.0
- BMW R 32 · Arnaud 25 · CC BY-SA 4.0
- Dixi 3/15 · Tobias Nordhausen · CC BY 2.0 (slides 1 and 2)
- BMW 1500 · Coolalabright · CC BY 4.0
- BMW iX3 · Matti Blume · CC BY-SA 4.0 (cropped to the car; the HQ tower is outside the frame)

The AI-generated images are FLUX.2 [pro], and each carries an "AI-generated" pill: `persona-china`, `persona-usa`, `cn-lwb`, `us-driver`. Their sidecars are in `Demo/03-images/*.json`.
App screens are crops of `Demo/04-recordings/stills/*.png`, plus one frame of `rec-04-l3-profiles.mp4` at 17.5 s (L1 principles). They live in `assets/crops/`.
No BMW logos are used, nor the M350 clip.

## Re-render
```bash
cd Demo/slides/_tools
npm install          # once: playwright 1.49.1 (uses system Chrome, falls back to bundled Chromium)
node render.mjs      # writes ../dixi-deck.pdf and pages/pNN.png, and reports any element that overflows a slide
./contact.sh         # PDF → pdfpages/*.png (pdftoppm) → ../_contact.png (ffmpeg)
pdfinfo ../dixi-deck.pdf | grep Pages   # must equal the slide count (16)
```

- BMW Group "100 years" PDF (R 32 and Dixi): https://www.press.bmwgroup.com/global/article/attachment/T0257819EN/354550/EN_BMW_Group_100_of_years_fascination_for_mobility.pdf
- 1945 pots and pans (secondary source): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_BMW
- China 5 Series long wheelbase, +12 cm: https://www.press.bmwgroup.com/global/article/detail/T0427958EN/the-new-bmw-5-series-sedan-and-the-new-bmw-i5-%E2%80%93-exclusively-from-china-for-china?language=en
- 2006 5 Series Li rear cooling box: https://www.press.bmwgroup.com/global/article/detail/T0009351EN/bmw-group-introducing-new-models-for-china?language=en
- "The Ultimate Driving Machine" since 1974: https://www.press.bmwgroup.com/usa/article/detail/T0447993EN_US/chapter-6:-%E2%80%9Cthe-ultimate-ad-slogan:-bmw-becomes-the-ultimate-driving-machine%E2%80%9D?language=en_US
- Repo: `backend/README.md` (backend planned, not built), `docs/architecture/04-build-plan.md` (Codebeamer ReqIF/CSV export, gap panel), `README.md` (L3 weights per series, PDF export).

## Image credits
History photos come from Wikimedia Commons. Each photo carries its credit on the slide.
- BMW IIIa · Wikisympathisant · CC BY-SA 4.0
- BMW R 32 · Arnaud 25 · CC BY-SA 4.0
- Dixi 3/15 · Tobias Nordhausen · CC BY 2.0 (slides 1 and 2)
- BMW 1500 · Coolalabright · CC BY 4.0
- BMW iX3 · Matti Blume · CC BY-SA 4.0 (cropped to the car; the HQ tower is outside the frame)

The AI-generated images are FLUX.2 [pro], and each carries an "AI-generated" pill: `persona-china`, `persona-usa`, `cn-lwb`, `us-driver`. Their sidecars are in `Demo/03-images/*.json`.
App screens are crops of `Demo/04-recordings/stills/*.png`, plus one frame of `rec-04-l3-profiles.mp4` at 17.5 s (L1 principles). They live in `assets/crops/`.
No BMW logos are used, nor the M350 clip.

## Re-render
```bash
cd Demo/slides/_tools
npm install          # once: playwright 1.49.1 (uses system Chrome, falls back to bundled Chromium)
node render.mjs      # writes ../dixi-deck.pdf and pages/pNN.png, and reports any element that overflows a slide
./contact.sh         # PDF → pdfpages/*.png (pdftoppm) → ../_contact.png (ffmpeg)
pdfinfo ../dixi-deck.pdf | grep Pages   # must equal the slide count (16)
```

content.text:
The deck is done: an HTML deck and a matching PDF, both 16 slides. The PDF has 16 pages at 1920×1080 px, so the page count equals the slide count. Nothing was committed or published, `git status` shows no new changes, and the deck makes no network calls.

**Files** (all in `/Volumes/PJ/peresjav/hackathons/ehl-final-minuch-2026/Demo/slides/`)
- `dixi-deck.html`: arrow keys, space, PageUp/PageDown, Home/End or click to move; slide counter in the footer; one slide per page when printed.
- `dixi-deck.pdf`
- `_contact.png`: all 16 PDF pages on one sheet. I checked it, plus full-size views of the math and human-gate slides. The render script's overflow check finds no text or element outside a slide.
- `README.md`: slide list, where each number comes from, sources, image credits, how to re-render.
- `assets/` holds the fonts, photos, AI images and screenshot crops; `_tools/` holds the render scripts (`render.mjs`, `contact.sh`).

**Slides**
1. Title: "Principled. Weighted. Traceable.", with the Dixi 3/15 photo
2. BMW has always adapted (1916, 1923, 1928, 1945, 1962, 2025)
3. Today the change is data
4. Same car, two best seats (China vs USA personas)
5. The workflow map, redrawn from the film's version
6. Layer 1: principles
7. Layer 2: evidence, scored (request list and the fridge detail)
8. A human decides, memory keeps it (reject dialog and decisions log)
9. The math: 75, 52 → 21, and 41/51/8 → 89
10. Layer 3: profiles, then the social test
11. Every weight is yours (AI proposes, PM applies, change log)
12. Same data, two answers
13. Every answer has a trail: comment → request → PM decision → profile
14. What we don't know yet
15. Running today, built to grow
16. Close: "btw, what was BMW's first car?" → "Dixi." and "BMW. The Ultimate Driving Machine.", credited as BMW's tagline since 1974

**Where I departed from your outline**
- **16 slides, not 12–14.** I gave source weights and the lineage chain their own slides (11 and 13) to keep one idea per slide. They could be folded back into slides 10 and 12.
- **Slide 12 shows the app's real US result, not the film's chips.** The film says "Ventilated seats / Larger trunk". The US best-fit profile (Tech-forward 89) is actually Sharper steering, CarPlay and head-up display, so the slide shows those. Slide 4 still uses the film's US persona chips.
- **The 1945 tile is text only.** There is no photo for it (the film uses video), and I left out the 1955 Isetta because it isn't among the facts you gave me.
- **The iX3 photo is cropped to the car** so the BMW HQ tower with its roundel is out of frame. Badges on the museum cars in the real photos are still visible, as in the film.
- **Slide 6 uses a frame from the profile recording** (rec-04 at 17.5 s), because there was no still of the principles.

**Not verified, or flagged as limits**
- "Pots and pans" in 1945 comes only from Wikipedia; it is cited as a secondary source on slide 2.
- I did not re-open the BMW web pages myself; I used the sources you listed and those already checked in `script.md`.
- The "What we don't know" gap cards exist only as example data on the landing page, not in the pipeline. Slide 14 says so.
- Codebeamer export and the FastAPI/Supabase backend are planned, not built, and are labelled that way on slide 15.
- The 89 on slide 9 works out to 88.6 with exact values (L2 = 518/618), and the slide shows rounded weights (0.414 / 0.506 / 0.08). The footnote says so.
